target.title: improve(google): identify OpenClaw Gemini API traffic
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw should be identifiable when it calls the Gemini API on a user's behalf. Today, those API-key requests do not include Google's documented partner/library attribution header, so Gemini traffic from OpenClaw is harder to distinguish from other client traffic.

AI-assisted: yes, implemented with Codex and reviewed locally.

## Why This Change Was Made

Google's Gemini API partner integration guidance asks partner and library integrations to send `x-goog-api-client` with a product/version token. This change adds `x-goog-api-client: openclaw/<version>` across OpenClaw's Gemini API paths, including direct REST calls, shared provider request policy, the GenAI SDK wrapper, embeddings, web search, video fallback, streaming, and prompt cache calls.

Authentication is intentionally unchanged. API-key calls still use `x-goog-api-key`, OAuth-style calls still use `Authorization: Bearer`, and the new attribution header is added alongside the existing auth headers.

## User Impact

Users do not need to change any settings. Operators and maintainers can expect Gemini API traffic from OpenClaw to carry OpenClaw attribution in the way Google asks partner integrations to identify themselves.

## Evidence

- `pnpm lint --threads=8`: passed.
- `pnpm run lint:extensions:bundled`: passed.
- `pnpm test:extension google`: 29 files, 403 tests passed.
- `pnpm vitest src/agents/provider-attribution.test.ts extensions/google/api.test.ts extensions/google/transport-stream.test.ts extensions/google/web-search-provider.test.ts extensions/google/google-genai-runtime.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/google-prompt-cache.test.ts`: 8 files, 212 tests passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: passed.
